
#Linear Models
```{r linearModels, include=TRUE}
m.base <- lm(weight ~ Time, data=d)
m.1 <- lm(weight ~ Time + Diet, data=d)
m.2 <- lm(weight ~ Time*Diet, data=d)
```

```{r comparelm, include = TRUE}
anova(m.base,m.1,m.2)
```
**Table 1:** Main effects and interaction linear models for Time and Diet.
```{r printLM table,echo=FALSE}
tab_model(m.base, m.1, m.2,
          digits = 3,
          show.df = T,
          show.stat = T,
          string.pred = "Ind. Variable",
          col.order = c("est","ci","df","stat","p"),
          dv.labels = c("Time", "Time+Diet", "Time*Diet"),
          pred.labels = c("Intercept", 
                          "Timepoint", 
                          "Diet 2",
                          "Diet 3",
                          "Diet 4",
                          "Timepoint*Diet 2",
                          "Timepoint*Diet 3",
                          "Timepoint*Diet 4")
          )
### Option: manually override the IV labels:
#tab_model(m.base, m.1, m.2, digits = 3, show.df = T, show.stat = T, string.pred = "Ind. Variable.", col.order = c("est","ci","df","stat","p"), dv.labels = c("Time", "Time+Diet", "Time*Diet"), pred.labels = c("Intercept", "Time", "Diet 2","Diet 3","Diet 4","Time*Diet 2","Time*Diet 3","Time*Diet 4"))
```
*Note:* The Statistic represent the t-statistic used to obtain the p-value using Satterthwaite's approximation. CI = the 95% confidence interval of the Estimate.

#Mixed Effects Models
```{r mixedModels, include=TRUE}
### trying random intercepts by Diet
mm.base <- lmer(weight ~ Time + (1 | Chick), data=d, REML=F)
mm.1 <- lmer(weight ~ Time + Diet + (1 | Chick), data=d, REML=F)
mm.2 <-lmer(weight ~ Time * Diet + (1 | Chick), data=d, REML=F)
anova(mm.base,mm.1,mm.2)
```

**Table 2:** Final main effects and interaction mixed models for Time and Diet.
```{r printMM table,echo=FALSE}
tab_model(mm.base, mm.1, mm.2,
          digits = 3,
          show.df = T,
          show.stat = T,
          string.pred = "Fixed Effect",
          col.order = c("est","ci","df","stat","p"),
          dv.labels = c("Time", "Time+Diet", "Time*Diet"),
          pred.labels = c("Intercept", 
                          "Timepoint", 
                          "Diet 2",
                          "Diet 3",
                          "Diet 4",
                          "Timepoint*Diet 2",
                          "Timepoint*Diet 3",
                          "Timepoint*Diet 4")
          )
```
 *Note:* The Statistic represent the t-statistic used to obtain the p-value using Satterthwaite's approximation. CI = the 95% confidence interval of the Estimate.


\newpage
```{r plotSave, include = TRUE}
 ### Build figure. Using dashed lines to emphasize breaks between time points. Here, each individual's line is plotted as raw data, so there are no error bars.
 ggplot(d, aes(x=Time, y=weight, group = Chick, color = factor(Diet))) +
  stat_summary(fun=mean, geom="point") +
   stat_summary(fun=mean, geom="line", linetype = 2) +
   labs(x="Time (days)", y="Weight (g)") +
   scale_fill_discrete(name = "Diet") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 15) 

### The same data grouped by diet. The fun.data plus "pointrange" options in stat_summary allow you to designate a mean and standard error within the grouping variable.
 ggplot(d, aes(x=Time, y=weight, color = factor(Diet))) +
   stat_summary(fun.data=mean_se, geom="pointrange") +
   stat_summary(fun=mean, geom="line", linetype = 2) +
   labs(x="Time (days)", y="Weight (g)") +
   scale_fill_discrete(name = "Diet") +
   theme_bw(base_size = 15)

 ### Export figure to a pdf.
 ggsave("TimeByDiet.pdf", width=5, height=5, dpi=300)
```
